subject: chemistry
question_text: A carbon compound on analysis gave the following percentage composition: carbon 14.5%, hydrogen 1.8%, chlorine 64.46%, oxygen 19.24%. Calculate the empirical formula of the compound.

verification.note: Chapter 5 (Stoichiometry) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.66-72), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 2+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Arithmetic re-checked: C₂H₃Cl₃O₂ back-computes to 14.5% C, 1.8% H, 64.4% Cl, 19.3% O — consistent with the given data. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25 (audit round 3): step s2_whole is TITLED Whole-number ratio while its mark_note says ×2 to whole numbers, and step s1_moles already ends with a ratio line that is not whole-number — a reader can mis-assign that step-1 line to step 2. The s2 why now states that the mark is for the doubling only. CROSS-CARD MARK-MAP DIFFERENCE, recorded for a teacher to settle: the move divide everything by the smallest value sits INSIDE the 2-mark step s1_moles on st_ef_c2h3cl3o2 and st_ef_k2cr2o7, but is the whole of the 1-mark step s2_ratio on st_ef_chcl3. The same piece of working therefore carries a different mark weight on the two card shapes. Nothing was moved — mark_split is the authority on each card, and both splits are still unconfirmed claims. No mark moved; no marked line changed.

steps.label: Relative moles of each element
lines: Divide each percentage by the atomic weight:
steps.why: Four elements means four divisions, but the method is unchanged: percent over atomic weight gives relative moles, then everything over the smallest value.
common_mistakes: Rounding 1.5 to 1 or 2 at this stage. Keep 1.5 — the next step fixes it honestly.
steps.memory_tip: Percent over atomic weight, then everything over the smallest — the same two moves for any number of elements.
steps.margin_note: Both marks are here: the four divisions and the division by 1.20.

steps.label: Whole-number ratio
lines: 1.5 is not a whole number, so multiply the
steps.why: Subscripts must be whole numbers. A ratio ending in .5 becomes whole when every term is doubled — rounding 1.5 to 1 or 2 would change the chemistry. Read the step title with care: the ratio 1 : 1.5 : 1.5 : 1 is already written at the end of step 1 and is not a whole-number ratio, so repeating it here earns nothing. This mark is for the doubling alone, which turns it into 2 : 3 : 3 : 2.
common_mistakes: Rounding 1.5 to 2 instead of multiplying the whole ratio by 2.
Multiplying only the 1.5 terms and leaving the 1s unchanged.
steps.memory_tip: A .5 in the ratio always means multiply EVERYTHING by 2.
steps.margin_note: The doubled ratio 2 : 3 : 3 : 2 earns this mark.

steps.label: The empirical formula
lines: The atoms are in the ratio C₂H₃Cl₃O₂.
steps.why: The whole-number ratio 2 : 3 : 3 : 2 written as subscripts in the element order C, H, Cl, O gives the empirical formula.
common_mistakes: Scrambling the subscript order between Cl and O.
Calling it the molecular formula — no molecular weight was given.
steps.memory_tip: Keep the elements in the order of the working table so the subscripts cannot swap.
steps.margin_note: Box C₂H₃Cl₃O₂ and name it the EMPIRICAL formula.

insider_note: The 1.5 in the ratio is the whole question: the examiner is watching for the multiply-by-2 step, and any rounding of 1.5 collapses the answer.
